work: The Metamorphoses of Ovid, Books I-VII + VIII-XV

Jupiter.what: Jupiter strikes down the Giants with lightning when they pile mountains toward heaven.
Jupiter summons the gods and declares he will destroy mankind.
Jupiter is tested by Lycaon, burns his house and condemns all men.
Jupiter sends the South Wind and rain to drown the world.
Jupiter hurls a thunderbolt and kills Phaëton to save the world.
Jupiter disguises himself as Diana and rapes Calisto.
Jupiter becomes a white bull and carries Europa over the sea.
Jupiter burns Semele with thunder and saves Bacchus in his thigh.
Jupiter answers Æacus's prayer by turning ants of the oak into men.
Jupiter carries Hercules' immortal part up to the stars.

Apollo.what: Apollo kills the serpent Python with arrows and founds the Pythian games.
Struck by Cupid's arrow, Apollo chases Daphne, who becomes a laurel.
Phœbus swears an oath to Phaëton and vainly warns him about the chariot.
Apollo kills Coronis in rage, repents, and rescues his unborn child.
Apollo accidentally kills Hyacinthus with a discus and turns his blood into a flower.
Apollo wins the music contest against Pan and gives Midas ass's ears.

Juno.what: Juno demands the heifer from Jupiter and sets Argus to guard Io.
Juno turns Calisto into a bear and has the stars barred from the sea.
Juno disguised as Beroë persuades Semele to ask Jupiter for his full majesty.
Juno blinds Tiresias after he sides with Jupiter.
Juno descends to the underworld and sends Tisiphone to madden Athamas and Ino.
Juno has Lucina delay Alcmena's labour until Galanthis tricks them.

Venus.what: Caught by the Sun, Venus takes revenge by making him love Leucothoë.
Venus urges Cupid to strike Pluto with love.
Venus turns the Cerastæ into bulls and the Propœtides into stone.
Venus brings Pygmalion's ivory statue to life.
Wounded by Cupid, Venus loves Adonis and gives Hippomenes golden apples.
Venus mourns Adonis and turns his blood into a flower.
Venus wins Æneas's deification and anoints him as a god.
Venus pleads for Caesar, then makes his soul a star.

Bacchus.what: Bacchus is born from Jupiter's thigh and hidden by the Nymphs.
Disguised as a boy, Bacchus turns his kidnappers into dolphins.
Bacchus turns the Minyeides' looms to vines and the sisters into bats.
Bacchus turns the Thracian women who killed Orpheus into trees.
Bacchus grants Midas the golden touch and then relieves him of it.

Diana.what: Diana discovers Calisto's pregnancy at the pool and banishes her.
Diana turns Actæon into a stag, and his hounds kill him.
Diana hides Arethusa in a cloud and turns her into a stream.
Angered by neglect, Diana sends the Calydonian boar.
Diana demands Iphigenia's sacrifice and substitutes a hind.

Mercury.what: Mercury tells the tale of Pan and Syrinx.
Mercury lulls Argus to sleep and beheads him.
Mercury steals Apollo's cattle and turns Battus into a touchstone.
Mercury falls in love with Herse and bargains with Aglauros.
Mercury drives the king's herd to the shore where Europa plays.
Mercury and Jupiter are welcomed by Baucis and Philemon.

Neptune.what: Neptune looses the rivers and strikes the earth with his trident.
Neptune lays down his trident and has Triton recall the waters.
Neptune makes Ino and Melicerta sea gods.
Neptune changes Perimele into an island.
Neptune builds Troy's walls, then floods the land and sends a monster.
Neptune turns his son Cygnus into a swan.
Neptune begs Apollo to avenge Cygnus by killing Achilles.

Naiads.what: The Naiads, forgetting Acheloüs, are swept into the sea and become islands.
The Naiads fill Acheloüs' broken horn with fruit and flowers.

Ceres.what: Ceres searches the world for Proserpina and turns a mocking boy into a lizard.
Ceres blights Sicily and appeals to Jupiter for her daughter.
Ceres sends Triptolemus to spread grain and turns Lyncus into a lynx.
Ceres sends Famine against Erisicthon for felling her sacred oak.

Cupid.what: Cupid shoots Apollo with a gold arrow and Daphne with a lead one.
Cupid shoots Pluto in the breast at Venus's request.

Ulysses.what: Ulysses wins Achilles' arms and fetches Philoctetes and the arrows.
Ulysses receives the winds in a bag, which his crew opens.
Ulysses uses moly to overcome Circe and frees his men.

Pallas.what: Minerva orders Envy to infect Aglauros with jealousy.
Pallas advises Cadmus to sow the dragon's teeth.
Pallas contests Arachne at weaving and turns her into a spider.

Aeneas.what: Aeneas flees Troy and is hosted by Anius at Delos.
Æneas is received by Dido in Libya and sails on past the Sirens.
Aeneas visits the underworld with the Sibyl to see his father.
Æneas defeats Turnus and is made a god.

Theseus.what: Theseus is saved from Medea's poisoned cup when Ægeus recognizes his sword.
Theseus kills the Minotaur with Ariadne's thread and deserts her on Dia.
Theseus joins the Calydonian boar hunt.
Theseus is stopped by the flooded Acheloüs and hears his tales.
Theseus rescues Hippodame and kills Eurytus at Pirithoüs' wedding.

Hercules.what: Hercules defeats Acheloüs in wrestling, tearing off his horn.
Hercules shoots Nessus, suffers the poisoned tunic, and is raised to the stars.
Hercules rescues Hesione, is cheated, and sacks Troy.
Hercules destroys Pylos and kills Nestor's brothers.
Hercules appears in dreams commanding Myscelos to leave Argos.

Pluto.what: Pluto inspects Sicily and is struck by Cupid's arrow.
Pluto abducts Proserpina and splits the earth to descend.
Pluto and Persephone yield to Orpheus's song and release Eurydice.

Nymphs.what: Diana's Nymphs expose Calisto's pregnancy at the bath.
The Nymphs judge the Muses victors over the Pierides.

Æacus.what: Æacus refuses Minos, aids Cephalus and tells of the plague.
Æacus prays to Jupiter and receives the Myrmidons from ants.

Atlas.what: Atlas refuses Perseus shelter and is turned into a mountain.

Priam.what: Priam is killed at the altar as Troy falls.

Acheloüs.what: Acheloüs shelters Theseus and tells of the Echinades and Perimele.
Acheloüs tells of Erisicthon and shows his lost horn.
Acheloüs wrestles Hercules, changing to serpent and bull, and loses a horn.

Achilles.what: Achilles is born to Peleus and Thetis.
Achilles strangles the invulnerable Cygnus, who becomes a swan.
Paris's arrow, guided by Apollo, kills Achilles.
Achilles' ghost demands the sacrifice of Polyxena.

Circe.what: Circe poisons Scylla's bay and turns her into a monster.
Circe turns Macareus' men into swine and is overcome by Ulysses.
Circe, spurned by Picus, turns him into a woodpecker.

Minerva.what: Minerva keeps Ericthonius in a basket and takes the crow as companion.
Minerva, angered at Aglauros, goes to Envy's cave.
Minerva turns Medusa's hair into snakes.
Minerva visits the Muses on Helicon.
Minerva saves Perdix by turning him into a partridge.

Aurora.what: Aurora begs Jove to honour her slain son Memnon.

Cadmus.what: Cadmus follows the heifer and prepares a sacrifice, sent by Agenor.
Cadmus kills the dragon, sows its teeth and founds Thebes.
Cadmus flees Thebes and becomes a serpent with his wife.

Minos.what: Minos prepares war to avenge Androgeus.
Minos is refused by Æacus at Ægina.
Minos rejects Scylla and her stolen lock and sails away.
Minos pays his vow and has Dædalus build the labyrinth.

Earth.what: God separates the elements and ends the discord of Chaos.
Earth turns the Giants' blood into a new race of men.
Scorched Earth pleads with Jupiter to save the universe.

Hector.what: Hector kills Protesilaüs at the Trojan landing.

Latona.what: Latona appeals to Apollo and Diana against Niobe's scorn.
Refused water, Latona curses the Lycian rustics into frogs.

Peleus.what: Peleus holds Thetis through her changes and weds her.
Peleus is exiled, welcomed by Ceyx, and wolf is turned to marble.

Proserpine.what: Proserpina is seized by Pluto while gathering flowers.
Proserpine turns Ascalaphus into an owl for revealing her pomegranate seeds.
Persephone as queen of shades yields to Orpheus.

Phaëton.what: Taunted by Epaphus, Phaëton sets out to find his father.
Phaëton demands the Sun's chariot and loses control of the horses.
Struck by Jupiter's thunderbolt, Phaëton falls into the Eridanus.
Phaëton is buried by the Naiads.

Agamemnon.what: Agamemnon, king and father of Iphigenia, leads the fleet at Aulis.
Agamemnon has the leaders judge the contest for Achilles' arms.
Agamemnon's fleet waits in Thrace as Achilles' ghost demands Polyxena.

Cephalus.what: Cephalus seeks Æacus's aid from Athens.
Cephalus tests Procris, is reconciled and receives dog and javelin.
Cephalus accidentally kills Procris with his javelin.

Mars.what: A dragon sacred to Mars lurks in the cave near Cadmus's sacrifice.
Mars is caught with Venus in Vulcan's net.

Lucina.what: Lucina, corrupted by Juno, delays Alcmena's labour until Galanthis tricks her.
Lucina helps Myrrha's tree open and Adonis is born.

Iris.what: Iris purifies Juno after her descent to the underworld.
Iris goes to the cave of Sleep at Juno's command.
Iris consoles Hersilia, who becomes Ora.

Jason.what: Jason wins the Golden Fleece with Medea's help.
Jason begs Medea to rejuvenate his father Æson.
Jason remarries, and Medea takes revenge.

Orpheus.what: Orpheus loses Eurydice, charms the underworld, and looks back.
Orpheus plays on a bare hill and draws the trees.
Orpheus begins his song of youths loved by gods.
Thracian women murder Orpheus, and his ghost rejoins Eurydice.

Sun.what: The Sun hides his face in grief for Phaëton.
The Sun exposes Venus and Mars, then loves Leucothoë and tricks his way in.
The Sun fails to revive Leucothoë and abandons Clytie.

Telamon.what: Telamon wakes Æacus to see the new Myrmidon men.
Telamon receives Hesione after Hercules sacks Troy.

Tethys.what: Tethys and Ocean agree to bar the stars from their waters.
Tethys turns Æsacus into a diving bird.

Themis.what: Themis's oracle tells Deucalion and Pyrrha to throw their mother's bones.
Themis prophesies coming Theban wars and Calirrhoë's sons.

Ægeus.what: Ægeus recognizes Theseus's sword and strikes the poisoned cup away.

Agenor.what: Agenor sends Cadmus to find Europa and forbids his return without her.

Io.what: Io, turned heifer, is guarded by Argus and writes her name in the dust.
Io is tormented by a Fury, restored and worshipped as a goddess.
Isis tells Telethusa to raise her daughter and later turns Iphis into a man.

Proteus.what: Proteus prophesies Thetis's son will surpass his father; Jupiter yields her.
Proteus advises Peleus to bind Thetis through her changes.

Scylla.what: Scylla cuts her father's lock for Minos, is rejected and becomes Ciris.
Scylla flees the sea god Glaucus.
Poisoned by Circe, Scylla becomes a monster and then a rock.

Clymene.what: Clymene swears the Sun is Phaëton's father and sends him off.
Clymene searches the earth and finds her son's bones.

Coronis.what: The crow tells how Minerva made her a bird escaping Neptune.
Coronis is shot by Apollo and dies after revealing her pregnancy.

Europa.what: Europa trusts the white bull and is carried across the sea.

Medusa.what: Perseus's tale of Medusa's beheading and her snaky hair.
Medusa's head petrifies Phineus and his followers.

Hecate.what: Medea meets Jason at Hecate's altar and gives him herbs.
Medea invokes Hecate for her midnight rejuvenation rite.

Mulciber.what: Vulcan forges a net and traps Venus and Mars before the gods.

Lycaon.what: Lycaon serves human flesh to Jupiter and is turned into a wolf.

Medea.what: Medea debates with herself, then pledges to help Jason with her herbs and charms.
Medea rejuvenates Æson with herbs and a cauldron after a nine-day flight.
Medea tricks Pelias's daughters into killing their father and throws him in the cauldron.
Medea burns the palace, kills her sons and escapes in a dragon chariot.
Medea prepares aconite for Theseus, but Ægeus knocks the cup away and she escapes.

Phocus.what: Phocus receives the Athenians and asks Cephalus about his strange javelin.

Perseus.what: Perseus turns Atlas into a mountain bearing the sky after being refused shelter.
Perseus finds Andromeda chained, kills the sea monster and wins her hand.
Perseus tells at the wedding feast how he killed Medusa.
Perseus fights Phineus's band, then petrifies Phineus and his men with the Gorgon's head.
Perseus turns King Polydectes to stone with Medusa's head.

Adonis.what: Adonis is born from the myrrh tree and anointed by the Naiads.
Venus falls in love with Adonis and warns him against fierce beasts.
Adonis ignores the warning, wounds a boar and is killed by it.

Aglauros.what: Aglauros unties Minerva's basket, which the crow reports.
Aglauros demands gold from Mercury for helping him with Herse.
Poisoned by Envy, Aglauros blocks Mercury's way and is turned to stone.

Alcmena.what: Alcmena recalls her seven days of labour and Galanthis's trick that frees her.

Arethusa.what: Arethusa tells Ceres that Proserpine is queen in the underworld.
Arethusa flees Alpheus, is turned into a stream and flows to Ortygia.

Athamas.what: Maddened by Tisiphone, Athamas kills his son Learchus and Ino flees.

Boreas.what: Boreas, refused Orithyïa, uses force and carries her off to Thrace.

Chiron.what: Chiron receives Apollo's rescued unborn child.
Chiron's daughter Ocyrrhoe foretells his painful death and teaching of Æsculapius.

Cinyras.what: Cinyras unknowingly lies with his daughter Myrrha, then chases her with a sword.

Cyane.what: Cyane bars Pluto's way, protesting, and dissolves into her pool in grief.
Cyane's pool shows Proserpine's girdle to Ceres.

Cygnus.what: Cygnus boasts of invulnerability, is strangled by Achilles and turned into a swan.

Dædalus.what: Dædalus builds the labyrinth for the Minotaur.
Dædalus makes wings, warns Icarus, and buries him after his fall.

Dryads.what: The Dryads appeal to Ceres for vengeance on Erisicthon after he fells the oak.

Echion.what: Echion is one of five earth-born survivors who help Cadmus build Thebes.

Glaucus.what: Glaucus tells how a magic grass turned him into a sea god, and woos Scylla.
Glaucus asks Circe for a charm and refuses her love; Scylla is transformed.

Herse.what: Mercury falls in love with Herse as she returns from Minerva's festival.

Hymenaeus.what: Hymenaeus presides at Iphis's wedding after his transformation.
Hymenaeus attends Orpheus's wedding with a smoking torch and ill omens.

Ino.what: Ino helps tear Pentheus apart on Cithaeron.
Fleeing Athamas, Ino leaps into the sea and becomes a goddess.

Iole.what: Iole tells Alcmena the story of her sister Dryope's transformation.

Macareus.what: Macareus meets Achæmenides and tells of Æolus's winds and the Læstrygons.
Macareus narrates how Circe turned his crew into swine and Ulysses saved them.

Nestor.what: Nestor tells of Cæneus and the battle of Lapithæ and Centaurs.
Nestor recounts how Hercules destroyed Pylos and killed his brothers.

Numa.what: Numa travels to Crotona to study the nature of things.
Numa becomes king and brings peace to Rome; after his death Egeria mourns him.

Ocean.what: Ocean and Tethys agree to bar Calisto's stars from their waters.

Pan.what: Pan pursues Syrinx and makes pipes from the reeds she becomes.
Pan challenges Apollo to a piping contest and loses.

Paris.what: Paris, guided by Apollo, shoots the arrow that kills Achilles.

Phineus.what: Phineus bursts into the wedding feast, attacks Perseus and is turned to stone.

Pirithoüs.what: Pirithoüs's wedding erupts into the battle of Centaurs and Lapithæ.

Procris.what: Procris tests Cephalus, flees to Diana, and returns giving him dog and javelin.
Procris spies on Cephalus in the woods and is killed by his javelin.

Semele.what: Tricked by Juno as Beroë, Semele asks Jupiter to appear in full majesty.
Semele is burned to ashes by Jupiter's thunder.

Tiresias.what: Tiresias judges for Jupiter, is blinded by Juno and given prophecy.
Tiresias warns Pentheus he will be torn apart if he rejects Bacchus.

Triton.what: Triton blows his shell to recall the floodwaters.

Typhœus.what: Typhœus lies pinned beneath Sicily, his struggles shaking the earth.

Actæon.what: Actæon stumbles on Diana bathing, becomes a stag and is killed by his hounds.

Aeetes.what: Aeetes sets Jason deadly tasks for the Golden Fleece.

Æsculapius.what: The infant Æsculapius is foretold as a healer by Ocyrrhoe.
Æsculapius comes to Rome as a serpent and ends the plague.

Diomedes.what: Diomedes refuses to aid Turnus and tells of Agmon turned into a bird.

Ajax.what: Ajax pleads for Achilles's arms, loses to Ulysses and kills himself.

Alcithoë.what: Alcithoë, weaving, lists tales she will skip and promises a novelty.

Amphion.what: Amphion kills himself after Apollo shoots his sons.

Anchises.what: Anchises is carried from Troy by Aeneas and questions Anius at Delos.
Anchises is seen as a ghost by Aeneas in the underworld.

Andromeda.what: Andromeda is chained to a rock, rescued by Perseus and married to him.

Antiphates.what: Antiphates and the Læstrygons destroy the Greek ships.

Arachne.what: Arachne refuses Pallas's warning and weaves the gods' loves in a flawless tapestry.
Beaten by Pallas, Arachne hangs herself and becomes a spider.

Argus.what: Argus guards Io, the heifer, for Juno with his hundred eyes.
Mercury lulls Argus to sleep and beheads him.

Atalanta.what: Atalanta first wounds the Calydonian boar; the spoils spark Meleager's quarrel.
Atalanta races her suitors and loses to Hippomenes's golden apples.
Atalanta and Hippomenes are turned into lions by Cybele.

Augustus.what: Jove foretells Augustus's rise, and Ovid prays for his long life.

Midas.what: Midas asks for the golden touch, nearly starves, and washes in the Pactolus to be freed.
Midas judges Pan above Apollo and is given ass's ears, which his barber betrays.

Cænis.what: Cænis, violated by Neptune, is made an invulnerable man, Cæneus, and later buried under trees and turned into a bird.

Calisto.what: Calisto is raped by Jupiter disguised as Diana, then exposed at the bath and banished.
Juno turns Calisto into a bear; Jupiter sets her and Arcas in the sky.

Calliope.what: Calliope is chosen to sing against the Pierides and begins her song.

Meleager.what: Meleager leads the boar hunt, kills the boar and his uncles, and dies when Althæa burns the brand.

Cepheus.what: Cepheus promises Andromeda to Perseus and rejoices at the monster's death and the wedding.
Cepheus reproaches Phineus as the wedding feast turns into a riot.

Ceyx.what: Ceyx welcomes Peleus and tells of his brother Dædalion's transformation into a hawk.
Ceyx sails to Claros despite Halcyone's pleas and drowns in a storm; he becomes a kingfisher.

Clytie.what: Clytie betrays Leucothoë to her father, is shunned by the Sun, and becomes a flower facing him.

Sibyl.what: The Sibyl guides Aeneas to the underworld and tells how Phoebus's bargain left her aging.

Cybele.what: Cybele turns Hippomenes and Atalanta into lions for profaning her shrine.
Cybele saves the Trojan ships from Turnus's fire by turning them into sea nymphs.

Deïanira.what: Deïanira is the prize in the wrestling contest between Hercules and Acheloüs.
Deïanira is carried off by Nessus, then sends the poisoned tunic to Hercules.

Deucalion.what: Deucalion survives the flood with Pyrrha and laments that they are all that remain of mankind.
Deucalion solves Themis's oracle; the stones he and Pyrrha throw become people.

Echo.what: Echo, cursed by Juno, loves Narcissus, is rejected and wastes away to a voice.
Echo repeats Narcissus's sorrow and last farewell as he dies.

Mænades.what: The Thracian Mænades tear Orpheus apart and are turned into oak trees.

Pierides.what: The nine Pierides challenge the Muses and sing of the gods hiding in animal forms.
The defeated Pierides abuse the Muses and are turned into magpies.

Envy.what: Envy, eating vipers, is ordered by Minerva to poison Aglauros with jealousy.

Epaphus.what: Epaphus mocks Phaëton about his divine father, prompting his journey to the Sun.

Erectheus.what: Erectheus refuses Boreas's pleading suit for his daughter Orithyïa.

Erinnys.what: Tisiphone drives Athamas and Ino mad, causing the death of Learchus and Ino's leap.

Eurydice.what: Eurydice dies of a snake bite and is lost a second time when Orpheus looks back.
Eurydice is reunited with Orpheus's ghost in the fields of the blessed.

Eurytus.what: Eurytus's daughter Dryope is rooted and turned into a lotus tree before her family.
Eurytus, drunk, seizes the bride Hippodame and is killed by Theseus.

Galatea.what: Galatea tells of her love for Acis, whom Polyphemus crushes; she turns his blood into a river.

Ganymede.what: Jupiter, as an eagle, carries off Ganymede to be his cup-bearer.

Halcyone.what: Halcyone prays to Juno, hears of Ceyx's death from Morpheus, and is turned into a kingfisher.

Hecuba.what: Hecuba is carried off after Troy falls, taking Hector's ashes.
Hecuba finds Polydorus dead, blinds Polymnestor, and is turned into a barking dog.

Icarus.what: Icarus ignores his father's warning, flies too high and drowns when the wax melts.

Inachus.what: Inachus hides in his cavern, weeping for his lost daughter Io.
Inachus meets Io and learns who she is from her writing in the dust.

Iphis.what: Iphis, raised as a boy, loves Ianthe, despairs, and is turned into a man by Isis.
Iphis hangs himself at the door of the cruel Anaxarete.

Ismenus.what: Ismenus, Niobe's eldest son, is shot by Apollo.

Itys.what: Itys is killed by Progne and Philomela and served to Tereus.

Lælaps.what: Lælaps chases the Teumessian beast and both are turned to marble.

Laomedon.what: Laomedon cheats Apollo, Neptune and Hercules of their pay, bringing flood, monster and Troy's sack.

Lelex.what: Lelex tells how Jupiter and Mercury were welcomed by Philemon and Baucis.

Leucothoë.what: The Sun disguised as her mother enters Leucothoë's chamber and she yields.
Leucothoë is buried alive by her father and becomes a frankincense tree.

Melicerta.what: Ino leaps into the sea with Melicerta, who becomes the sea god Palæmon.

Narcissus.what: Narcissus is born, proud and beautiful, and spurns Echo and all suitors.
Narcissus falls in love with his reflection, wastes away and becomes a flower.

Astræa.what: Astræa, the last god on earth, abandons it in the Iron Age.

Thetis.what: Thetis is seized by Peleus through her shape-changes and bears Achilles; later she pleads for the wolf.

Nessus.what: Nessus carries off Deïanira, is shot by Hercules and gives her the poisoned tunic.

Niobe.what: Niobe scorns Latona, loses all her children and turns to weeping stone.
Hated by the people, Niobe is mourned for by her brother Pelops alone.

Polymnestor.what: Polymnestor murders Polydorus for his gold once Troy is ruined.
Lured by promised treasure, Polymnestor is blinded by Hecuba and the captive women.

Oeneus.what: Oeneus neglects Diana in his offerings, so she sends the boar on Calydon.

Orithyïa.what: Boreas, refused by Erectheus, seizes Orithyïa, carries her to Thrace, and she bears twins.

Pandion.what: Pandion gives Progne to Tereus, then tearfully entrusts Philomela to him.
Pandion dies of grief as his daughters become birds.

Peneus.what: Peneus's daughter Daphne prays to him and is turned into a laurel.
Peneus receives the neighbouring rivers at Tempe, who come to console or congratulate him.

Philoctetes.what: Philoctetes lights Hercules' pyre and receives his bow.

Philomela.what: Philomela is carried off by Tereus, raped, and has her tongue cut out.
Philomela weaves her story into a cloth and sends it to Progne.
Philomela is rescued by Progne and helps kill Itys.
Philomela throws Itys' bloody head at Tereus and is changed into a bird.

Polydorus.what: Polydorus is killed by Polymnestor for his gold.
Hecuba finds Polydorus' corpse on the shore and plans revenge.

Polyphemus.what: Polyphemus sings to Galatea, then crushes Acis with a rock.
Achæmenides recalls Polyphemus hurling rocks and devouring his companions.

Pomona.what: Pomona tends her orchard and rejects all suitors, including Satyrs and Priapus.
Pomona is won over when Vertumnus reveals his true form.

Progne.what: Progne marries Tereus, asks for her sister's visit, and learns of the crime by weaving.
Progne, as a Bacchante, rescues Philomela from captivity.
Progne kills her son Itys and serves him to Tereus.
Progne is changed into a swallow.

Prometheus.what: Prometheus fashions Man from earth and water in the gods' image.

Propœtides.what: The Propœtides deny Venus, become the first prostitutes and harden into stone.

Pyrrha.what: Pyrrha survives the flood with Deucalion on Parnassus.
Pyrrha prays at Themis's temple and hesitates over the oracle's command.
Pyrrha throws stones behind her, and they become women.

Python.what: Python, born of the earth, terrorizes mankind until Apollo kills him with arrows.

Romulus.what: Romulus is carried off by Mavors to become the god Quirinus.
Romulus' lance takes root and becomes a tree.

Raven.what: The once-white raven flies to tell Apollo of Coronis's infidelity.
The raven informs Apollo and is cursed to lose its white plumage.

Rhœtus.what: Rhoetus is struck down by the spear Perseus hurls back at Phineus.

Satyrs.what: The Satyrs mourn Marsyas, and their tears form the river Marsyas.

Silenus.what: Silenus, drunk, is captured by Phrygian peasants and feasted by Midas.

Tereus.what: Tereus wins Progne, lusts after Philomela, carries her off, rapes her and cuts out her tongue.
Tereus unknowingly eats his son Itys and pursues the sisters.
Tereus is changed into a crested lapwing.

Turnus.what: Turnus fires the Trojan ships, which Cybele turns into sea nymphs; he later dies.

Vertumnus.what: Vertumnus woos Pomona in many disguises, finally as an old woman.
Vertumnus tells of Anaxarete, reveals his true form and wins Pomona.

Achæmenides.what: Achæmenides, rescued by Aeneas, recounts his terror of Polyphemus to Macareus.

Acis.what: Acis, Galatea's beloved, is crushed by Polyphemus's rock and becomes a river.

Acoetes.what: Acoetes is seized by Pentheus, tells of the dolphin-sailors, and is freed from prison.

Æsacus.what: Æsacus pursues Hesperia, leaps from a cliff in grief and becomes a didapper.

Æson.what: Æson is made young again by Medea's rites and potion.

Æthon.what: Æthon and the sun's horses bolt from their track under Phaëton.

Agave.what: Agave, with her sisters, tears her son Pentheus apart, mistaking him for a boar.

Agmon.what: Agmon defies Venus and is turned into a bird with his companions.

Alphenor.what: Alphenor, a son of Niobe, is shot down by Apollo.

Alpheus.what: Alpheus pursues Arethusa across Arcadia to Elis, then becomes water to join her.

Althæa.what: Althæa learns Meleager killed her brothers and turns to vengeance.
Althæa burns the life-brand and Meleager dies; she then kills herself.

Amphissos.what: Dryope's infant Amphissos is the child for whom she picks the lotus.

Ampyx.what: Ampyx is turned to stone mid-thrust when Perseus shows the Gorgon's head.

Amycus.what: Amycus fights in the Centaur brawl, wielding a chandelier as a weapon.

Anaxarete.what: Anaxarete scorns Iphis, watches his funeral and is turned to stone.

Ancæus.what: Ancæus boasts, then is killed by the Calydonian boar.

Andræmon.what: Andræmon sees his wife Dryope rooted and covered with bark, and clings to her.

Anius.what: Anius welcomes Aeneas to Delos and tells how his daughters were seized and turned into doves.

Anius's daughters.what: Anius's daughters are seized by Agamemnon and changed into doves by Bacchus.

Antenor.what: Antenor rushes in to report the wolf slaughtering Peleus's herds.

Aphidas.what: Aphidas, a sleeping drunk Centaur, is killed by Phorbas in the brawl.

Apulian shepherd.what: The Apulian shepherd mocks the Nymphs and is turned into a wild olive.

Arcas.what: Arcas, fifteen, meets his bear-mother Calisto and nearly spears her; Jupiter sets both in the sky.

Ariadne.what: Ariadne helps Theseus with the thread, is deserted on Dia, and is comforted by Liber.

Asbolus.what: Asbolus, one of Actæon's hounds, helps tear apart his stag-shaped master.

Ascalaphus.what: Ascalaphus reveals that Proserpine ate pomegranate seeds and is turned into an owl.

Astyages.what: Astyages strikes Aconteus and is petrified by the Gorgon's head.

Athis.what: Athis, a beautiful Indian youth, is killed in the fighting at the wedding hall.

Romans.what: The Romans consult Delphi, send envoys to Epidaurus and welcome the serpent god at the Tiber.

Autonoe.what: Autonoe helps tear Pentheus apart on Cithaeron, mistaking him for a boar.

barber.what: The barber cannot keep Midas's secret and whispers it into a hole in the ground.

Battus.what: Battus sees Mercury steal the cattle and accepts a cow to stay silent.
Battus betrays the secret to the disguised Mercury and is turned into a touchstone.

Baucis.what: Baucis and Philemon welcome the disguised gods and prepare a poor but generous meal.
Baucis and Philemon are spared the flood, serve as priests, and become intertwined trees.

Byblis.what: Byblis falls in love with her brother Caunus and dreams of embracing him.
Byblis debates with herself and resolves to confess by letter.
Byblis writes to Caunus; he reads part, rages and sends the servant away.
Byblis keeps pressing Caunus until he flees his country.
Mad with grief, Byblis wanders after Caunus and dissolves into a spring.

Calaïs.what: Calaïs is born, a winged twin of Zethes, and later sails with the Minyæ.

Calchas.what: Calchas reads the serpent omen as nine years of war before Troy falls.
Calchas declares that Diana must be appeased with a virgin's blood.

Canace.what: Canace, one of Actæon's hounds, helps hunt down the stag-shaped Actæon.

Canens.what: Canens, singing wife of Picus, is loved by him and loved only by him.
Canens searches six days for Picus, laments by the Tiber and dissolves into air.

Caunus.what: Caunus reads Byblis's letter, rages, rejects her and flees his country to found a city.

Cerastæ.what: The Cerastæ of Amathus sacrifice strangers and are turned into bulls by Venus.

Cercopes.what: The perjured Cercopes are turned into speechless apes by Jupiter.

Chaos.what: Chaos is the formless, discordant mass of warring elements before God separates them.

Chione.what: Chione is violated by Mercury and Apollo, then killed by Diana for boasting.

Cippus.what: Cippus sees horns on his head and refuses kingship, choosing exile; Romans honour him.

Contriver of the World.what: The unnamed creator god shapes globe, seas, zones and winds, and sets the stars shining.

Crow.what: The crow warns the raven that his errand to Apollo is fruitless.

Cycnus.what: Cycnus mourns Phaëton by the Eridanus and is turned into a swan.

Cyparissus.what: Cyparissus accidentally kills his beloved tame stag and resolves to die of grief.
Inconsolable, Cyparissus is changed into the cypress by Phœbus.

Dædalion.what: Dædalion, mad with grief over Chione's death, is turned into a hawk by Apollo.

Daphne.what: Daphne, struck by Cupid's lead arrow, flees Apollo and prays to her father.
Daphne turns into a laurel, which Apollo adopts as his sacred tree.

Daughters of Minyas.what: The daughters of Minyas keep weaving through Bacchus's festival; their webs turn to ivy and vines.
Hiding from phantom fires and beasts, the sisters are changed into bats.

Dido.what: Dido receives Æneas in Libya, loves him and later kills herself on a pyre.

dragon.what: The dragon of Mars kills Cadmus's companions at the spring.
Cadmus fights the dragon and pins it through the throat to an oak.

Dryope.what: Dryope plucks lotus flowers that bleed and is rooted, covered with bark.
Dryope swears her innocence, entrusts her son to her family and says farewell.

Egeria.what: Egeria flees to Aricia and weeps for her dead husband Numa.
Egeria dissolves in tears and Diana turns her into a spring.

Ocyrrhoe.what: Ocyrrhoe, inspired, prophesies the fates of the infant Æsculapius and her father Chiron.
Forbidden to say more, Ocyrrhoe is turned into a mare called Enippe.

Eridanus.what: The river Eridanus receives the blazing Phaëton as he falls from the sky.

Erisicthon.what: Erisicthon fells Ceres' sacred oak, kills a man who resists, and ignores the dying Nymph's warning.
Cursed with Famine's hunger, Erisicthon devours his fortune, sells his daughter, and finally eats his own limbs.

Eurylochus.what: Eurylochus alone escapes Circe's swine-transformation and warns Ulysses.

Fame.what: Fame, in her brazen house of rumours, announces the coming Greek fleet to the Trojans.

Famine.what: Famine, found gaunt in Scythia by Oreas, receives Ceres' order to enter Erisicthon.
Famine breathes hunger into the sleeping Erisicthon.

The Fates.what: The Fates' decree tying Meleager's life to a brand is fulfilled when Althæa burns it.

Sleep.what: Sleep, in his dark cave, chooses Morpheus to carry the dream to Halcyone.

Fauns.what: The Fauns mourn Marsyas, and their tears form the river Marsyas.

Galanthis.what: Galanthis tricks Lucina into breaking her spell and is turned into a weasel.

Giants.what: The Giants pile mountains toward heaven; Jupiter's lightning topples them and their blood becomes men.

Gorge.what: Gorge is spared when Diana turns Meleager's other sisters into birds.

Minyae.what: The Argonauts reach Colchis; Jason, aided by Medea, wins the Fleece.

Hebe.what: Hebe makes Iolaüs young again, and Themis stops her swearing never to repeat it.

Hebrus.what: The Hebrus carries Orpheus's head and lyre, still sounding, down to the sea and Lesbos.

Heliades.what: The Heliades mourn Phaëton at his tomb, turn into poplars, and their tears become amber.

Hermaphroditus.what: Hermaphroditus bathes in Salmacis' pool, is seized by her, and is joined with her in one body.
Now two-sexed, Hermaphroditus prays that the spring weaken any man who bathes in it.

Hermione.what: Hermione flees Thebes with Cadmus, begs to share his fate, and becomes a serpent.

Hersilia.what: Hersilia is consoled by Iris and raised to the sky as the goddess Ora.

Hesione.what: Hesione is exposed to a sea monster, rescued by Hercules, and given to Telamon.

Hesperia.what: Hesperia flees Æsacus, is bitten by a snake and dies.

Hesperian Naiads.what: The Naiads bury Phaëton and carve his epitaph.

Hippodamas.what: Hippodamas hurls his pregnant daughter Perimele into the sea.

Hippodame.what: Hippodame is seized by drunken Eurytus at her wedding and rescued by Theseus.

Hippolytus.what: Slandered by his stepmother, Hippolytus is dragged to a mangled death by his horses.
Healed against Pluto's will, Hippolytus is hidden by Diana and renamed Virbius.
Virbius comforts Egeria with his story, then watches her turn into a spring.

Hippomenes.what: Hippomenes challenges Atalanta to a race and falls in love with her.
With Venus' golden apples, Hippomenes delays Atalanta and wins the race.
Forgetting Venus' help, Hippomenes is turned with Atalanta into lions by Cybele.

Hyacinthus.what: Hyacinthus hunts with Apollo, is struck by his rebounding quoit and dies.
Hyacinthus's blood becomes a flower inscribed with Apollo's grief; Sparta keeps his festival.

Hylonome.what: Hylonome dies on the weapon that killed her beloved Cyllarus.

Ianthe.what: Ianthe is betrothed to Iphis, and the two fall in love.

Ilioneus.what: Ilioneus, Niobe's youngest son, is shot down by Apollo with his brothers.

Iolaüs.what: Iolaüs appears made young again by Hebe, and Themis prophesies about him.

Iphigenia.what: Iphigenia is brought to the altar to be sacrificed; Diana substitutes a hind.

Julius Cæsar.what: Julius Cæsar is murdered in the Senate-house, and Venus turns his soul into a star.

Lampetie.what: Lampetie mourns Phaëton at his tomb and is rooted, turning into a poplar.

Latreus.what: Latreus mocks Cænis as a woman and is wounded by invulnerable Cæneus.

Picus.what: Picus, loved by Canens, rides out to hunt boar.
Picus refuses Circe's love out of faithfulness to Canens and is threatened.
Circe turns Picus into a woodpecker and his men into beasts.

Learchus.what: Learchus is dashed against stones by his maddened father Athamas.

Leuconoë.what: Leuconoë tells the tale of the Sun's loves, beginning with Venus and Mars.

Lichas.what: Lichas carries the poisoned tunic to Hercules.
Hercules hurls Lichas into the sea, where he becomes a rock.

Ligdus.what: Ligdus orders his wife Telethusa to kill any daughter born.

Liriope.what: Liriope bears Narcissus and hears the prophecy about his life.

Lotis.what: Dryope plucks the lotus, the transformed nymph Lotis, which bleeds.

Lycian countrymen.what: The Lycian countrymen refuse Latona water, muddy the pool, and become frogs.

Lyncides.what: Lyncides, an Æthiopian noble, explains to Perseus how Medusa got her snaky hair.

Lyncus.what: Lyncus tries to murder the sleeping Triptolemus and is turned into a lynx.

Manto.what: Manto commands the Theban women to honour Latona.

Marsyas.what: Marsyas loses a flute contest to Apollo and is flayed alive.

Memnon.what: Aurora pleads with Jove to honour her slain son Memnon.

Memnonides.what: The Memnonides rise from Memnon's pyre embers and fight each other yearly.

Menœtes.what: Menœtes is killed by Achilles, who is testing the invulnerable Cygnus.

Metra.what: Metra, Erisicthon's daughter, is sold repeatedly and escapes each time by changing shape.

Miletus.what: Miletus flees Crete from Minos and founds a city in Asia.

Minotaur.what: Theseus kills the Minotaur in the labyrinth.

Urania.what: Urania welcomes Minerva to Helicon and explains the magpies are the defeated Pierides.

Monychus.what: Monychus urges the Centaurs to bury Cæneus under trees.

Triptolemus.what: Triptolemus spreads Ceres' grain and escapes Lyncus's murder attempt in Scythia.

Mopsus.what: Mopsus hails the bird that rises from Cæneus's burial.

Morpheus.what: Sleep chooses Morpheus to carry the news of Ceyx's death.
Morpheus, in Ceyx's shape, tells Halcyone of his drowning.

Muses.what: The Muses win the singing contest judged by the Nymphs and endure the Pierides' abuse.

Myrmidons.what: The Myrmidons, men made from ants, appear in the palace and receive Æacus's city and lands.

Myrrha.what: Myrrha struggles with her passion for Cinyras, tries to hang herself, and is saved by her nurse.
Myrrha is brought to Cinyras in the dark; he discovers her and chases her with a sword.
Myrrha flees, prays to be neither living nor dead and becomes the myrrh tree, bearing Adonis.

Myscelos.what: Commanded by Hercules in dreams, Myscelos defies the law of Argos, is tried and acquitted by the turned pebbles.
Myscelos sails to Italy and founds Crotona.

Nisus.what: Nisus, king of Alcathoë, is betrayed when his daughter Scylla steals his purple lock.
Nisus, changed into a sea eagle, attacks his daughter Scylla, who becomes the bird Ciris.

Numicius.what: The river Numicius washes away Æneas's mortal part so Venus can make him a god.

nurse.what: The nurse stops Myrrha's suicide and arranges her nights with the drunken Cinyras.

Nyseian Nymphs.what: The Nyseian Nymphs hide and nurse the infant Bacchus.

Oreas.what: Oreas flies in Ceres' chariot to Scythia and orders Famine to enter Erisicthon.

Orphne.what: Orphne's son Ascalaphus is made an owl for revealing Proserpine's pomegranate seeds.

Paphos.what: Paphos is born to Pygmalion and the statue brought to life by Venus.

Pasiphaë's daughter.what: Falsely accuses Hippolytus; he is cursed by Theseus and dragged to a mangled death.

Pelias.what: Pelias's daughters are won over by Medea's ram trick.
Medea puts Pelias to sleep; his daughters stab him and she throws him in the cauldron.

Pelops.what: Pelops alone mourns his sister Niobe and shows his ivory shoulder.

Pentheus.what: Pentheus mocks Tiresias and rages against Bacchus, ordering Acoetes seized.
Pentheus has Acoetes tortured and jailed, but the doors and chains open themselves.
Pentheus spies on the rites at Cithaeron and is torn apart by Agave and her sisters.

Perdix.what: Perdix, Dædalus's gifted nephew thrown from Minerva's citadel, is saved as a partridge and mocks the burial.

Periclymenus.what: Periclymenus is shot by Hercules as an eagle, despite shape-changing.

Perimele.what: Perimele, pregnant, is hurled into the sea and changed into an island by Neptune.

Petræus.what: Petræus is killed in the battle of Centaurs and Lapithæ.

Pettalus.what: Pettalus, the musician, is killed in the slaughter in the hall.

Phædimus.what: Phædimus is shot dead by Apollo with his brothers.

Phaëthusa.what: Phaëthusa, eldest of the mourning sisters, is first to turn into a poplar.

Philemon.what: Philemon and Baucis welcome the disguised Jupiter and Mercury into their poor cottage.
Philemon and Baucis prepare a humble feast and try to kill their goose.
Philemon asks to be priest and die with Baucis, and the cottage becomes a temple.
Philemon and Baucis turn into intertwined trees.

Phlegon.what: Phlegon bolts with the sun's horses as Phaëton drops the reins.

Plexippus.what: Plexippus is killed by his nephew Meleager in a quarrel over the boar's spoils.

Polydectes.what: Polydectes denies Medusa is dead and is turned to stone by Perseus.

Polyxena.what: Polyxena is demanded by Achilles' ghost and dies bravely, asking to die free.

Prœtus.what: Prœtus, who seized Acrisius's citadel, is turned to stone by Perseus with the Gorgon's head.

Pygmalion.what: Pygmalion carves an ivory woman and falls in love with her.
Pygmalion prays at Venus's festival and the statue comes to life as his wife.

Pyramus.what: Pyramus and Thisbe whisper through the chink, plan to meet at Ninus's tomb, and both die by the sword.

Pyreneus.what: Pyreneus lures the Muses into his house, tries to force them, and falls to his death.

Pythagoras.what: Pythagoras teaches at Crotona against eating meat, on the migration of souls and universal change.

Salmacis.what: Salmacis falls in love with Hermaphroditus, seizes him while he bathes and prays never to be parted.
The gods merge Salmacis and Hermaphroditus into one two-sexed body.

soothsayer.what: The soothsayer reads Cippus's horns as an omen that he will be king.

South Wind.what: The South Wind is sent out with rain-laden wings to flood the earth.

Stellio.what: Stellio mocks the thirsty Ceres and is turned into a speckled lizard.

Syrinx.what: Syrinx flees Pan to the river Ladon and is changed into reeds.

Tages.what: Tages rises as a prophet from an Etrurian clod of earth.

Tarpeia.what: Tarpeia betrays the citadel to the Sabines.

Tatius.what: Tatius leads the Sabines in war against Rome.

Telethusa.what: Telethusa begs Ligdus in vain not to kill a daughter.
Isis tells Telethusa to raise the child; she raises the girl as a boy, Iphis.
Telethusa prays at Isis's altar and Iphis is changed into a man.

the boar.what: The boar gores Adonis to death.

the stag.what: The tame stag is accidentally killed by Cyparissus, who then grieves.

Thescelus.what: Thescelus is turned to stone by the Gorgon's head while hurling a javelin.

Thisbe.what: Thisbe talks with Pyramus through the wall, flees the lioness, and kills herself beside him.

Tlepolemus.what: Tlepolemus complains that Hercules is left out, prompting Nestor's bitter tale.

Tmolus.what: Tmolus judges the contest between Pan and Apollo and awards victory to Apollo.

Toxeus.what: Toxeus, a uncle of Meleager, seizes the spoils from Atalanta and is killed by Meleager.

Venulus.what: Venulus asks Diomedes for aid for Turnus, is refused, and passes the cave of the Nymphs.

Acrisius.what: Acrisius's citadel is seized by Proetus, whom Perseus turns to stone to avenge him

Tantalus.what: Tantalus's descendants suffer as Niobe boasts of her ancestry and her sons are slain

Autolycus.what: Autolycus is born to Chione and Mercury, a crafty thief

Cephisus.what: Cephisus overpowers Liriope and fathers Narcissus

Dictys.what: Dictys, a sailor in Acoetes's tale, is turned into a dolphin with the crew

Dorylas.what: Dorylas, a horned Centaur, is killed by Peleus in the Lapith battle

Lycabas.what: Lycabas, an exiled murderer, is among the sailors turned into dolphins
Lycabas, Athis's friend, is killed in the slaughter at the wedding hall

Nyctimene.what: Nyctimene is turned into an owl after incest with her father

Aconteus.what: Aconteus is petrified by accident when he sees the Gorgon's head

Aethalion.what: Aethalion takes the helm of the ship carrying the disguised Bacchus

Alcimedon.what: Alcimedon is a sailor in the crew turned into dolphins

Attis.what: Attis, follower of the Mother of the Gods, is recalled as the man changed into the pine.

Beroë.what: Juno takes the form of Beroë, Semele's nurse, and urges her to demand Jupiter's full majesty.

Charon.what: Charon refuses to ferry Orpheus across after Eurydice is lost the second time.

Creon.what: Creon's palace is burned by Medea, who destroys him and his daughter.

Cyllarus.what: Cyllarus, beautiful young Centaur, is killed in battle and his mate Hylonome dies with him.

Daughters of Pelias.what: Deceived by Medea, they stab and dismember their father Pelias for a false rejuvenation

Dryas.what: Dryas fights the Centaurs, wounding Rhœtus and killing many

Epidaurian elders.what: The Epidaurian elders debate whether to give up their god Æsculapius

Exadius.what: Exadius fights the Centaurs and blinds Gryneus

Gryneus.what: Gryneus hurls an altar at the Lapithæ and is blinded

Lelegeïan Nymphs.what: The Lelegeïan Nymphs try to comfort the grieving Byblis

Man.what: Man is formed by the gods, given an upright face to look at the stars

Neoptolemus.what: Neoptolemus wields the sword that kills Polyxena at Achilles' tomb

Ovid.what: Ovid prays for Augustus's long life and declares his poem will make him immortal

Protesilaüs.what: Protesilaüs is the first Greek to land at Troy and is killed by Hector.

Rhetenor.what: Rhetenor, defying Venus with Agmon, is turned into a bird.

serpent.what: A serpent lunges at Orpheus' floating head on Lesbos and is turned to stone.

Telemus.what: Telemus prophesies that Ulysses will take Polyphemus' eye.

Tiberinus.what: Tiberinus, king of Alba, drowns in the Etrurian river, which takes his name.
